- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for downward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged overshoot; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust quickly; apply a “sentiment lag” correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day of sentiment decay.
- Mean reversion bias: if price has been above 70–75 for 5+ days, model tends to overpredict; apply a “reversion floor” rule: cap forecast at 70–72 unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates early in the cycle (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or bullish.
